overall_rule: RED if the EJ indicator is RED or >=2 scored indicators are RED; GREEN if no RED and <=1 AMBER; else AMBER
headline: Pricey power, mixed burden, modest jobs

indicators.name: Population (census tract)
indicators.plain_english: About 1,542 people live in the neighbourhood tract around the site.
indicators.source: US Census Bureau ACS 5-year 2020-2024 Data Profiles DP03/DP04/DP05, tract 06085504602, via data.census.gov table API (https://data.census.gov/api/access/data/table?id=ACSDP5Y2024.DP03&g=1400000US06085504602)

indicators.name: Median household income (tract)
indicators.plain_english: A typical household here earns about $121,953 a year (151% of the US median $80,734).
indicators.rag_rule: tract median / US median: >=100% GREEN, 75-100% AMBER, <75% RED (low-income areas feel power-bill and rent pressure more)
indicators.source: US Census Bureau ACS 5-year 2020-2024 Data Profiles DP03/DP04/DP05, tract 06085504602, via data.census.gov table API (https://data.census.gov/api/access/data/table?id=ACSDP5Y2024.DP03&g=1400000US06085504602)

indicators.name: Poverty rate (tract)
indicators.plain_english: About 8 in 100 people live below the federal poverty line.
indicators.source: US Census Bureau ACS 5-year 2020-2024 Data Profiles DP03/DP04/DP05, tract 06085504602, via data.census.gov table API (https://data.census.gov/api/access/data/table?id=ACSDP5Y2024.DP03&g=1400000US06085504602)

indicators.name: Unemployment rate (tract)
indicators.plain_english: About 5.3 in 100 people in the labour force are out of work.
indicators.rag_rule: <4% GREEN (tight labour market, hard to hire), 4-7% AMBER, >=7% RED (community need, jobs promises scrutinised)
indicators.source: US Census Bureau ACS 5-year 2020-2024 Data Profiles DP03/DP04/DP05, tract 06085504602, via data.census.gov table API (https://data.census.gov/api/access/data/table?id=ACSDP5Y2024.DP03&g=1400000US06085504602)

indicators.name: Renter households (tract)
indicators.plain_english: About 27 in 100 homes are rented, so more neighbours are exposed to rent and bill changes.
indicators.rag_rule: <35% GREEN, 35-55% AMBER, >=55% RED (renters have less control over costs and less stake in property-tax gains)
indicators.source: US Census Bureau ACS 5-year 2020-2024 Data Profiles DP03/DP04/DP05, tract 06085504602, via data.census.gov table API (https://data.census.gov/api/access/data/table?id=ACSDP5Y2024.DP03&g=1400000US06085504602)

indicators.name: Median age (tract)
indicators.plain_english: Half the residents are younger than 48.
indicators.rag_rule: 30-50 GREEN else AMBER; context, not scored
indicators.source: US Census Bureau ACS 5-year 2020-2024 Data Profiles DP03/DP04/DP05, tract 06085504602, via data.census.gov table API (https://data.census.gov/api/access/data/table?id=ACSDP5Y2024.DP03&g=1400000US06085504602)

indicators.name: Median household income (Santa Clara County)
indicators.plain_english: Across Santa Clara County, a typical household earns about $164,281.
indicators.source: US Census Bureau ACS 5-year 2020-2024 Data Profiles DP03/DP04/DP05, county 06085, via data.census.gov table API (https://data.census.gov/api/access/data/table?id=ACSDP5Y2024.DP03&g=0500000US06085)

indicators.name: Retail electricity price, commercial (CA)
indicators.plain_english: Businesses in CA pay about 26.2 cents per kWh for power (commercial customers).
indicators.rag_rule: industrial: <7 GREEN, 7-12 AMBER, >=12 RED; commercial: <9 GREEN, 9-15 AMBER, >=15 RED (operating-cost risk, not community risk)
indicators.source: EIA Electricity retail-sales API v2 (https://api.eia.gov/v2/electricity/retail-sales/), state annual average price

indicators.name: Retail electricity price, industrial (CA)
indicators.plain_english: Businesses in CA pay about 21.0 cents per kWh for power (industrial customers).
indicators.rag_rule: industrial: <7 GREEN, 7-12 AMBER, >=12 RED; commercial: <9 GREEN, 9-15 AMBER, >=15 RED (operating-cost risk, not community risk)
indicators.source: EIA Electricity retail-sales API v2 (https://api.eia.gov/v2/electricity/retail-sales/), state annual average price

indicators.name: Energy burden, low-income households (Santa Clara County)
indicators.plain_english: Lower-income households here spend about 3% of their income on home energy (6% or more is considered high).
indicators.rag_rule: DOE high-burden threshold 6%: >=6 RED, 4-6 AMBER, <4 GREEN
indicators.source: DOE/NREL LEAD Tool 2022 data (OpenEI submission 6219, https://data.openei.org/submissions/6219), ACS-based; computed here as sum(energy cost)/sum(income) over households at <=80% area median income
indicators.note: all households in county: 1.0%; low-income households in the tract: 3.08% (small ACS sample, noisy)

indicators.name: CalEnviroScreen 4.0 overall percentile (tract)
indicators.plain_english: This neighbourhood is more pollution-burdened and vulnerable than about 67% of California neighbourhoods.
indicators.rag_rule: >=75 (state 'disadvantaged community' line, SB 535) RED, 50-75 AMBER, <50 GREEN; high burden = community-acceptance risk
indicators.source: OEHHA CalEnviroScreen 4.0, CalEPA/OEHHA ArcGIS layer CES4_Percentile (https://oehha.ca.gov/calenviroscreen/report/calenviroscreen-40)
indicators.note: pollution-burden percentile 82, population-characteristics percentile 50; locale San Jose

indicators.name: Permanent data-center jobs per 100 MW
indicators.plain_english: A 100 MW data center employs only about 20-40 people once built.
indicators.rag_rule: <50 permanent jobs per 100 MW = AMBER (small direct local employment benefit)
indicators.source: Hamm Institute data-center workforce forecast, Nov 2025 (20-30 per 100 MW) and Latitude Media benchmark (25-40 per 100 MW for automated campuses); both seen via a secondary roundup, not re-verified
indicators.note: estimate; Uptime Institute figures cited elsewhere are higher (100-200 ops roles per 100 MW hyperscale campus)

indicators.name: Peak construction workers per 100 MW
indicators.plain_english: Building 100 MW needs roughly 70-200 workers on site at the busiest point, for about 1.5-3 years.
indicators.source: Chmura Economics article citing a workforce study of 0.7-2.0 peak direct construction workers per MW (underlying study not located; unverified)
indicators.note: Apollo Technical 2026 tracker reports ~4.1 per MW at campus peak (median of 19 campuses), so the real number could be about 2x higher

indicators.name: Property-tax contribution per 100 MW (estimate)
indicators.plain_english: A 100 MW data center might pay roughly $12 million a year in property tax before any abatement or equipment depreciation.
indicators.rag_rule: AMBER while abatements and equipment depreciation are unknown; GREEN needs a signed agreement showing net payments above $5M/yr per 100 MW
indicators.source: California: 1% Prop 13 base rate plus voter-approved debt, about 1.15% of assessed value in San Jose Unified (Santa Clara County Assessor tax-rate compilation); Prop 13 limits assessed value to purchase price +2%/yr. Assumes $1.0B taxable value per 100 MW (illustrative, not sourced).
indicators.note: order of magnitude only; real bills are lower after server depreciation and any negotiated abatement
